column2: On the authority of Abū Yaʿlā Shaddād ibn Aws (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), who said:

“Allah has prescribed excellence (iḥsān) in everything. So when you kill, kill well; and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let each of you sharpen his blade and let him spare suffering to the animal he slaughters.” Reported by Muslim.
ʿAlā kulli shayʾ (“in everything”): ʿalā here has the sense of ilā (“towards”) or fī (“in”).
“So when you kill”: in retaliation or as a prescribed punishment,
“kill well (fa-aḥsinū al-qitlah)”: by choosing the easiest, lightest way that takes life most quickly. Al-qitlah is with kasrah on the qāf.
“And when you slaughter”: those animals that may lawfully be slaughtered,
“slaughter well”: by being gentle with the animal, sharpening the instrument, facing it towards the qiblah, mentioning the name of Allah, and intending by slaughtering it to draw near to Allah.

Wa-l-yuḥidda (“let him sharpen”): with ḍammah on the yāʾ, from aḥadda al-sikkīn (“he sharpened the knife”), or with fatḥah, from ḥadda. Shafratahu (“his blade”), with fatḥah on the shīn: the instrument of slaughter.
Wa-l-yuriḥ (“let him spare suffering”): with ḍammah on the yāʾ.
Dhabīḥatahu (“the animal he slaughters”): the animal slaughtered; the pattern faʿīlah in the sense of mafʿūlah.

The command to excellence, which in everything is according to it. Excellence in performing the outward and inward obligations is performing them in a way that completes their obligatory parts; this degree of excellence in them is obligatory.

Excellence by completing their recommended parts is recommended. Excellence in leaving the unlawful is refraining from it and leaving both its outward and its inward forms; this degree is obligatory. Excellence in patience with what is decreed is being patient with it without resentment or panic.
The obligatory excellence in dealing with people and living among them is fulfilling the rights of theirs that Allah has made obligatory.
The obligatory excellence in having authority over people is fulfilling among them the obligations of legitimate authority.

Excellence in killing those animals that may lawfully be killed is taking their life in the quickest, easiest and most merciful way, without adding to the torment, for that is pain for which there is no need.

The prohibition of what the people of the Jāhiliyyah used to do: mutilating in killing, by cutting off noses and ears, hands and feet; slaughtering with blunt knives and the like, which torments the animal; and their eating of animals that had been strangled, and the others mentioned with it in the verse of al-Māʾidah.
